_contract: What may and may not be reused if a Phase-C2 behavioural session is interrupted. Registered BEFORE the run it governs, because a reuse rule written after seeing a result is a rule chosen by the result. AUTHORIZES NOTHING.
why_this_exists: Twelve probes is ~27 hours of L40S. An interruption part-way through is likely enough that the reuse question will be asked under time pressure, and that is the worst moment to decide it. AGENTS.md is explicit that preservation is not permission: saving a checkpoint authorizes nothing about reusing it, and whether preserved work may be pooled or resumed is a separate scientific decision governed by the experiment's retry policy.

the_unit_of_reuse.unit: one probe: one arm trained from one initialization under one seed
the_unit_of_reuse._a_record_is_not_a_checkpoint: a journal entry claiming a probe finished is not the probe. Reuse re-derives the identity from the bytes on disk through `identify_for_transfer` and refuses anything that does not match what was announced — at the destination when the probe lands, again on the host before a continuation ships it, and again on the replacement pod from the bytes that arrive there. Without that, a replacement resource could substitute for a measurement.
the_unit_of_reuse._the_descriptor_decides: the journal's record is self-consistent by construction, so checking it against itself proves nothing about whether it is the probe the rung asked for. The comparison that means something is against the descriptor the schedule builds from the frozen protocol.

rules.rule: A probe may be reused ONLY within the same scientific campaign id, and the campaign id is not the run attempt.
rules.why: the twelve probes are ONE experiment. A replacement pod is a new RESOURCE and a new run attempt inside the same campaign, so it may continue with that campaign's completed probes; a probe from a DIFFERENT campaign is a different experiment, and silently mixing two experiments' work would make the executed design something nobody preregistered and the mixture would be invisible in the result.

rules.rule: A probe may be reused only when its bytes still re-identify to the artifact_digest that was announced when it finished.
rules.why: the bytes decide. A directory that is gone, truncated or overwritten is not a completed probe.

rules.rule: A completed probe is NEVER retrained.
rules.why: retraining a finished probe and keeping whichever result is preferred is selection on the outcome. It does not become acceptable because the first result was disappointing.
rules._how: the rung loop continues past any probe already present in `self.scores`, which only the campaign journal populates. There is no flag that forces a retrain.

rules.rule: No ranking until all six screening results exist.
rules.why: ranking a partial field selects on who happened to finish first, which is a different experiment from the preregistered one.
rules._how: checked at the end of stage S and again at the start of stage R, so neither a resumed nor a fresh run can rank a partial field.

rules.rule: No verdict from a partial confirmation field. All six confirmation probes must exist before the decision rule runs.
rules.why: the estimand is a paired difference over three seeds; a verdict from four probes is not the preregistered quantity.
rules._how: refuses any field that is not exactly six probes covering exactly the three frozen seeds with both arms present.

rules.rule: A resumed session re-materializes its arms rather than trusting a staged copy, unless that copy re-identifies to the pinned digest; and it restores completed probes from the durable destination rather than expecting the previous resource's filesystem to still exist.
rules.why: arms are cheap to rebuild and are digest-pinned at every step, so trusting an unverified copy would be the one place a substituted initialization could enter the experiment. Probes are not cheap to rebuild and may not be rebuilt at all, so they travel from the only copy that survived the previous resource.

rules.rule: A continuation must consume its campaign's probes as the probes the rung asks for: probe id, rung, arm, seed and initialization digest must match the descriptor, and the training configuration must be identified.
rules.why: re-identifying the bytes proves the file is what was announced. It does not prove the file is this arm's measurement. Without the descriptor comparison, a probe trained from a different initialization could stand in for one of the twelve.

rules.rule: Screening commits ONCE per campaign. Once the advanced candidate is mechanically committed, a later run attempt must confirm that same candidate and may not rerun screening for another outcome.
rules.why: screening is deterministic from six scores, so a recomputation should agree — and 'should' is the word that makes it worth checking. A continuation that ranked again and advanced a different candidate would be selecting on which attempt survived.
rules._how: stage R recomputes the ranking, refuses when it disagrees with the committed record, and then advances the COMMITTED candidate. Neither result is discarded: both are evidence and the disagreement goes to review.

rules.rule: A replacement resource may not launch while a previous resource of the campaign is unreconciled, and may not launch when settled campaign spend plus its own planned all-in exceeds the campaign's approved all-in ceiling.
rules.why: at most one resource of a campaign may bill at a time, and the budget is cumulative across every resource and subrun. An unknown billing state is itself a stop condition.

rules.rule: A continuation is budgeted on the work the campaign still OWES — its incomplete probes, the arms those probes need rebuilt on a fresh filesystem, and the restore of its verified probes — never on a fresh full session.
rules.why: reserving a whole session per attempt refused every continuation by construction: with a ceiling sized for one session, any prior spend above $0 made settled + reserved exceed it. Pricing the remainder is what makes the cumulative rule usable instead of merely safe.
rules._how: behavioural.session_decomposition prices remaining work, and a fresh campaign's remaining work is all of it, so the full session and every continuation come from ONE derivation. A completed probe is never priced again; a complete campaign owes nothing and may not continue at all.
rules._fail_closed: if the remainder does not fit the approved campaign ceiling the gate refuses and returns to the maintainer. The experiment is not shortened to fit and the ceiling is not raised.

what_a_resume_may_never_do: pool probes across CAMPAIGNS, which are different experiments
substitute a probe that does not match the rung's descriptor
retrain a completed probe for a different outcome
rerun screening for a different advanced candidate
rank, advance or decide on a partial field
substitute a functionally similar checkpoint for an identity mismatch
extend the seed set, add a tie-break rung, or force a winner
continue after a complete valid scientific verdict
launch while a previous resource of the campaign may still be billing
spend past the campaign's cumulative approved all-in ceiling
admit a restored probe whose bytes do not reproduce its announced identity at the new local path
treat the previous resource's filesystem as still existing
budget a continuation as though no probe had been completed
if_a_campaign_cannot_be_completed: stop and report. A behavioural selection that trained nine of twelve probes has no verdict and must not be presented as having a partial one. The nine preserved probes are evidence about what was trained, not about which candidate wins. Whether a fresh campaign may reuse them is a maintainer decision, and this document's default answer is NO.
_pre_science_retries_are_different: an invocation that aborts BEFORE formal training begins produced no measurement to retry. AGENTS.md P12.1 permits diagnosing, repairing and retrying that under a fresh attempt identity inside the same cumulative budget. This document governs the case where training HAS begun.

campaign_versus_resource.campaign_is: ONE 12-probe scientific experiment: six screening probes, one mechanical ranking, six confirmation probes, one verdict. It is bound by the grant and the authorization, which name this campaign and no other.
campaign_versus_resource.run_attempt_is: ONE launcher invocation and the provider resource it draws. It is unique per invocation and per resource, and it exists so logs, evidence, spend and teardown can be attributed to the resource that produced them.
campaign_versus_resource._the_correction: an earlier version of R1 said 'a replacement pod is a new campaign'. That was wrong, and it made this document's own continuation policy unreachable: the launcher passed the run id as the campaign id, so a replacement resource could not consume a single probe the previous resource had trained and verified off-pod. A replacement pod is a new RESOURCE and a new run attempt INSIDE THE SAME scientific campaign. Consuming its predecessor's destination-verified probes is continuation of one preregistered experiment, not pooling across experiments.
continuation_conditions: the probe's identity matches the descriptor this rung derives from the frozen protocol and the six materialized arms: same probe id, rung, arm, seed and initialization artifact digest, and an identified training configuration
the destination bytes still re-identify to the artifact identity that was announced when the probe finished
the previous resource is PROVIDER-CONFIRMED non-billing; a zero return code on a remove call is not evidence of release
cumulative campaign spend, settled across every prior resource and run attempt plus this session's planned all-in, remains inside the campaign's approved all-in ceiling
the probe's bytes and its score evidence are restored to the replacement resource from the durable destination and re-identified there, at the new local path, before the campaign journal admits them
campaign_versus_resource._cumulative_means_cumulative: the approved all-in ceiling bounds the CAMPAIGN, not each resource. A rerun does not reset it and a replacement resource does not receive a fresh allocation. A continuation that does not fit refuses at the gate; funding a campaign for more than one full session is a maintainer decision.

how_a_replacement_resource_gets_the_prob.why_this_needed_saying: the campaign id alone made the policy expressible, not reachable. A replacement pod has a FRESH FILESYSTEM: the previous pod's audit/probes/*.json is gone and every model_dir it recorded points at nothing, and those two things are exactly what the driver's journal reads. The only surviving copy is the durable destination on the launcher host.
how_a_replacement_resource_gets_the_prob.transport: the launcher's materialize_inputs step — after setup, before the driver starts, and the pod is torn down if it fails — pushes each eligible probe's bytes and science evidence from the durable destination to a NEW path on the replacement pod, together with a small manifest naming that path and the identity to reproduce there.
how_a_replacement_resource_gets_the_prob.eligibility: only probes whose durable_ack.json records a destination-side re-identification that MATCHED. The launcher re-identifies them AGAIN on this host before sending, because an ack is a record and a record is not a checkpoint, and the driver re-identifies them a third time from the bytes that land on the pod.
how_a_replacement_resource_gets_the_prob.why_the_bytes_and_not_just_the_identitie: a probe trained but not validly scored resumes AT SCORING under R2, and scoring reads the weights. A manifest of identities would leave such a probe unscoreable, and R3 forbids retraining it.
how_a_replacement_resource_gets_the_prob.cost: the restore is billed pod time — any scp to a pod happens after it exists — bounded at the slowest recorded dev-box uplink, 0.23 MB/s, so one 1.11 GiB probe is about 80 minutes. Those minutes are a phase in the remaining-work bound R10 checks, so a restore that does not fit the campaign ceiling is refused before a pod exists. A maintainer freeing Hugging Face private storage would move this to the $0 pre-pod relay and remove the minutes; that is a maintainer decision.
how_a_replacement_resource_gets_the_prob.the_old_path_is_not_the_truth: the producing pod's model_dir is not carried as a directive. The driver's journal records the new local path, after verifying it.
